paragraphs.title: The Drought and Elijah’s Retreat to the Brook Cherith

easy.explanation: Elijah told Ahab that there would be neither dew nor rain except according to his word.
easy.q: To whom did Elijah announce that there would be no dew or rain?

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan.
easy.q: Where did the Lord command Elijah to hide?

easy.explanation: The ravens brought Elijah bread and flesh in the morning and evening.
easy.q: Who brought Elijah bread and flesh?

answers: There had been no rain in the land
The ravens drank all its water
medium.explanation: The brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
medium.q: Why did the brook dry up?

answers: He went and did according to the word of the Lord
medium.explanation: Elijah obeyed the Lord and dwelt by the brook Cherith.
medium.q: What did Elijah do after the Lord commanded him to go to Cherith?

answers: To provide for and feed you
medium.explanation: The Lord said that the ravens would provide Elijah with food there.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “sustain thee” mean in this passage?

answers: The lack of rain eventually caused the brook to dry up
The brook caused the rain to stop
There was no relationship between them
challenge.explanation: The drought announced by Elijah led to the drying up of the brook.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between Elijah’s announcement and the drying of the brook?

answers: The brook gave him water and the ravens brought him food
challenge.explanation: The Lord provided Elijah with water from the brook and food from the ravens.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the Lord cared for Elijah during the drought?

answers: The Lord gave instructions and then gave new instructions when circumstances changed
Elijah always acted without the Lord’s command
The Lord commanded Elijah to remain at the brook after it dried up
challenge.explanation: The Lord first sent Elijah to Cherith and later sent him elsewhere after the brook dried up.
challenge.q: What does the order of events show about the Lord’s guidance of Elijah?

paragraphs.title: The Widow of Zarephath and the Request for Food

answers: To Zarephath, which belonged to Zidon
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Elijah to go to Zarephath, which belonged to Zidon.
easy.q: Where did the Lord send Elijah?

easy.explanation: Elijah met a widow woman gathering sticks.
easy.q: Who was the woman Elijah met at the gate of the city?

easy.explanation: Elijah asked her to fetch a little water in a vessel.
easy.q: What did Elijah first ask the widow to bring him?

medium.explanation: Elijah also asked her to bring him a morsel of bread.
medium.q: What did Elijah ask for after the widow went to fetch water?

answers: She did not know who he was
She had only a handful of meal and a little oil
medium.explanation: The widow had only a small amount of meal and oil left for herself and her son.
medium.q: Why did the widow find it difficult to give Elijah bread?

medium.explanation: She was collecting sticks to prepare the last food for herself and her son.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “gathering of sticks” show the widow was doing?

answers: She was gathering sticks while he was searching for water
He asked for food even though she had almost no food herself
They had both come from the king’s palace
challenge.explanation: Elijah requested water and bread from a woman who had only a final small supply of food.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in Elijah’s meeting with the widow?

answers: Her lack of food was extremely serious
challenge.explanation: Her words show that she believed her remaining food would soon be gone.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the widow’s plan to eat and die?

challenge.explanation: Elijah first requested water and then asked for a morsel of bread.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Elijah’s requests?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Flour and Oil

answers: The bread brought by the ravens
easy.explanation: The widow was to use the small amount of meal and oil that she had.
easy.q: What did Elijah ask the widow to use in making him a little cake?

answers: The barrel of meal and the cruse of oil
easy.explanation: Elijah promised that the meal would not waste and the oil would not fail.
easy.q: What did Elijah promise would not fail?

answers: Elijah, the widow, and her household
easy.explanation: The widow, Elijah, and her household ate for many days.

medium.explanation: Elijah told her to make him a little cake first.
medium.q: What did Elijah ask the widow to do “first”?

answers: Until the Lord sent rain upon the earth
medium.explanation: The supply would last until the Lord sent rain upon the earth.
medium.q: How long did Elijah say the meal and oil would last?

medium.explanation: A cruse was a small container holding the oil.
medium.q: What was a “cruse” in this passage?

answers: She refused to listen to him
She obeyed Elijah despite her difficult situation
challenge.explanation: She did according to Elijah’s saying even though she had very little food.
challenge.q: What did the widow’s action after Elijah’s words show?

answers: The promise did not come true
The widow found food somewhere else
The meal did not waste and the oil did not fail according to the word of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage states that the promised provision continued exactly as the Lord had spoken.
challenge.q: How is the promise connected to its result?

answers: She feared that there would not be enough food for her and her son
challenge.explanation: The promise addressed her fear that her small supply of food would soon be exhausted.
challenge.q: Why was the promise of the meal and oil a direct answer to the widow’s situation?

paragraphs.title: The Son’s Illness and Elijah’s Prayer

easy.explanation: The son of the woman who owned the house fell sick.

answers: That he had come to bring her sin to remembrance and slay her son
That the brook had filled again
easy.explanation: The widow asked whether Elijah had come to call her sin to remembrance and kill her son.
easy.q: What did the widow say to Elijah?

easy.explanation: Elijah carried the child up into a loft and laid him on his own bed.
easy.q: Where did Elijah carry the child?

answers: He sent the child to the brook
He asked the widow for sticks
medium.explanation: Elijah prayed to the Lord concerning the child.
medium.q: What did Elijah do after carrying the child into the loft?

medium.explanation: Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times.
medium.q: How many times did Elijah stretch himself upon the child?

answers: Caused harm or trouble to come upon
medium.explanation: Elijah asked whether the Lord had brought this tragedy upon the widow by slaying her son.
medium.q: In Elijah’s prayer, what does “brought evil upon” mean?

answers: His arrival came before the illness, and she interpreted the events as connected
Elijah had said that he would kill her son
challenge.explanation: The widow connected Elijah’s coming with the tragedy that followed.
challenge.q: Why did the widow think Elijah’s presence was connected with her son’s death?

answers: Let the child’s soul come into him again
Send him away from the city
challenge.explanation: Elijah asked the Lord that the child’s life might return to him.
challenge.q: What did Elijah ask the Lord to do in his prayer?

answers: He returned the child to his mother and then carried him away
He took the child, carried him up, and laid him on his bed
He sent the child to the brook and then prayed
challenge.explanation: Elijah took the child from his mother, carried him to the loft, and laid him on his bed.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Elijah’s actions?

paragraphs.title: The Child Returns to Life and the Widow’s Recognition

answers: The child’s soul came into him again, and he revived
easy.explanation: The child’s soul returned to him, and he lived again.
easy.q: What happened after the Lord heard Elijah’s voice?

easy.explanation: Elijah brought the child down and delivered him unto his mother.
easy.q: To whom did Elijah give the child?

answers: That he was a man of God
That he lived by the brook
easy.explanation: The woman said that she now knew Elijah was a man of God.
easy.q: What did the woman recognize about Elijah?

answers: That the word of the Lord in Elijah’s mouth was truth
That the rain had already returned
medium.explanation: She recognized that the Lord’s word spoken by Elijah was true.
medium.q: What else did the woman recognize at the end of the event?

answers: He delivered the child to his mother
He returned him to the brook
He left him in the loft
medium.explanation: Elijah brought the child down and gave him to his mother.
medium.q: What did Elijah do after the child revived?

medium.explanation: The return of the child’s soul describes the return of his life.
medium.q: In this context, what does “soul” refer to?

answers: From suspicion and accusation to recognition of his divine commission
From indifference to leaving the city
challenge.explanation: She first accused Elijah, but later recognized him as a man of God.
challenge.q: How did the widow’s attitude toward Elijah change?

answers: The child revived after Elijah’s prayer
challenge.explanation: The child’s return to life confirmed the truth of the Lord’s word spoken through Elijah.
challenge.q: What strengthened the woman’s statement that the word of the Lord in Elijah’s mouth was truth?

answers: The Lord heard Elijah, and the widow recognized the truth of God’s word
The prayer failed, and the widow left
The widow prayed while Elijah remained silent
challenge.explanation: After the Lord answered Elijah’s prayer, the widow acknowledged the truth of his message.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Elijah’s prayer and the widow’s response?
